$description:
Elevation — the only place a shadow may be defined. Four component CSS files previously wrote raw rgb(0 0 0 / x) shadows inline, which is the same class of error as a hardcoded hex: it cannot be re-themed, and it is wrong in dark mode by construction. A shadow is a light-source model, and a black shadow assumes a light surface. These are semantic, and elevation.dark.json overrides them.

The levels are named for what is raised, not for how far: a contributor asking 'how much shadow does a menu get' should not have to guess between `lg` and `xl`.

raised.$description: Cards and panels — sitting on the page, not over it. Two layers because one shadow cannot be both a tight contact edge and a soft ambient falloff, and a single-layer shadow is the most reliable tell of an unconsidered system.

overlay.$description: Menus, popovers, dialogs — genuinely above the page and dismissible. Deeper than `raised` because the gap it implies is real: you can click through to what is underneath.

knob.$description: The travelling part of a control — a switch knob, a slider thumb. Single-layer and tight on purpose: it has to read as attached to the track it slides along, not floating over it.
